title: How to watch the UEFA Champions League on Prime Video outside the US
summary: Exclusive matches, advanced stats, and an all-star punditry team—here's your guide to the Champions League on Prime Video outside the U.S.
body_markdown:
---


## **Key takeaways**


- A top-pick UEFA Champions League match airs every matchday on Prime Video in select countries outside the U.S.


- Coverage is presented by talent including Wayne Rooney, Mats Hummels, and Luca Toni.


- Prime Vision offers an enhanced viewing experience with advanced statistics and AI-powered insights.


---


The UEFA Champions League is the biggest club competition in European football, and in select countries outside the U.S.,


[Prime](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/amazon-prime) members can watch it live on


[Prime Video](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/tag/prime-video) —with dedicated coverage, local-language commentary, and expert pundits in every market.


[How to watch live sports like the NBA, NFL, and more on Prime Video](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/entertainment/live-sports-streaming-prime-video)


Prime members can also watch New York Yankees, Duke men's basketball, NWSL, and regional NHL games in 2026.


Here's everything you need to know about how to watch the UEFA Champions League on Prime Video outside the U.S.


## Where can I watch the UEFA Champions League on Prime Video?


Prime Video broadcasts the UEFA Champions League in the following countries:


- United Kingdom & Ireland:


The top-pick match every Tuesday exclusively on Prime Video at no additional cost, plus all remaining fixtures available via add-on subscription.


- Germany:


The top-pick match every Tuesday exclusively on Prime Video at no additional cost, plus all remaining fixtures available through the DAZN add-on subscription on Prime Video.


- Italy


: The top-pick Wednesday match exclusively on Prime Video at no additional cost.

## Who presents the UEFA Champions League on Prime Video?


Prime Video's UEFA Champions League coverage features dedicated broadcast teams across each country, bringing local-language commentary and expert analysis from some of football's most recognizable names.


- United Kingdom & Ireland:


Gabby Logan leads the coverage alongside former Champions League winners Wayne Rooney and Daniel Sturridge, with Jon Champion and Alan Shearer on commentary.


- Germany:


Presenter Jonas Friedrich is joined by commentator Hannes Herrmann, co-commentator Benedikt Höwedes, and experts including Mats Hummels, Matthias Sammer, Chris Kramer, Tabea Kemme, and Josephine Henning.


- Italy:


Giulia Mizzoni and Marco Cattaneo host the coverage, with Mizzoni live from the pitch and Cattaneo in the Prime Video studio. Sandro Piccinini and Massimo Ambrosini provide commentary, and the expert panel includes Claudio Marchisio, Julio Cesar, Fernando Llorente, Gianfranco Zola, and Luca Toni.


## What is Prime Vision?


Prime Vision is a brand-new alternate match feed available on Prime Video—an additional way for fans to watch UEFA Champions League football, layered with advanced statistics, real-time insights, and on-screen graphics.


It's designed to give viewers a deeper, data-driven perspective on the tactics powering European football's most prestigious competition. Many of the metrics Prime Vision brings to the broadcast—the same kind used by professional clubs, scouting departments, and data platforms—have never been available inside a live match before.


Prime Vision will continue to evolve throughout the season, and beyond, shaped by fan feedback and new AI-powered innovations that will bring even more features and insights to the viewing experience.


The alternate feed builds on the learnings from Prime Vision's introduction during


NFL Thursday Night Football


in 2022.


[Amazon’s custom AI-powered Prime Insights take fans inside the game](https://www.aboutamazon.com/stories/prime-video-ai-live-sports-viewers-tv)


Real-time analytics powered by custom Amazon AI models bring expert-level insights to Thursday Night Football, NASCAR, and NBA viewers.


Here's what Prime Vision offers:


- Tactical Map:


All 22 player positions are tracked in real time, so you can see how a team is structured, track how a winger is pressuring the fullback, and observe tactical shifts as they happen.


- Momentum:


A momentum bar calculates the probability that either team will score in the next 10 seconds, using metrics like possession, player positioning, and chances created to show the cumulative threat a team has posed over the last five minutes.


- Physical Insights:


Track and compare the physical output of the world's greatest players in real time, including running speed, jump height, shot speed, and pass distances.


- Advanced Analytics:


Access to cutting-edge metrics traditionally used by clubs and data analysts, including expected goals (xG), shot quality (xGOT), expected pass (xPass), and expected save (xSave).


- Passing Options:


Using a player's positioning, direction, and viewing angle, Prime Vision highlights the three most likely passing options—allowing you to anticipate where the ball could go before the pass is made.


- Player ID:


A nametag overlay identifies the player in possession, which is especially useful in European competition where you might be watching unfamiliar teams and squads.


To access Prime Vision, fans can select the alternate feed from the match detail page or in-game by pressing down on the remote.


## What is Dynamic Standings in the Champions League?


Dynamic Standings is integrated into the main broadcast experience on Prime Video.


It allows fans to see live league table updates across all Champions League fixtures as the action unfolds—helping viewers understand exactly where every team sits in the League Phase in real time.


To use it, simply press up on your remote, navigate to the Stats menu, and select Standings card from the in-game menu.


The table includes clear markers for:


- Automatic qualification spots:


Teams progressing directly to the Round of 16


- Playoff positions:


Teams heading into a two-legged knockout playoff


- Elimination zone:


Teams facing exit from the competition


It's a simple but powerful addition that puts the full picture of the Champions League at your fingertips while you watch.


## How does the UEFA Champions League format work? League Phase and knockouts explained


At the start of the 2024-25 season, the UEFA Champions League underwent its biggest structural change in decades.


The traditional group stage—where 32 teams were drawn into eight groups of four—has been replaced by an expanded League Phase featuring 36 teams competing in a single league table.


The new format uses what's known as a Swiss model. Rather than playing the same three opponents home and away, each team is drawn against eight different opponents and plays eight matches—four at home and four away.


All 36 teams are ranked together in one table based on points, goal difference, and goals scored.


Here's how the League Phase standings break down:


- 1st–8th place:


Automatically qualify for the Round of 16 knockout stage.


- 9th–24th place:


Enter a two-legged knockout play-off round, with the winners advancing to the Round of 16.


- 25th–36th place:


Eliminated from the competition.


Because multiple matches take place simultaneously and every result affects the single league table, the final matchdays can be particularly dramatic—with qualification, play-off places, and elimination all on the line at the same time.


From the Round of 16 onward, the competition shifts to a straight knockout format—two-legged ties through the quarterfinals and semifinals, before a single match decides the final.
